Not every dog can do this, and not every trainer can or should. With the owners' permission, I used Bishop to help communicate a lesson to Ryder. Dogs naturally understand other dogs better than they understand us. The goal wasn't to make Ryder love every dog she sees-it was to teach her that she doesn't need to react to every dog she sees. Before training, a simple neighborhood walk was nearly impossible. Seeing another dog meant lunging, pulling, and trying to start conflict. Through obedience work and carefully controlled sessions with Bishop, Ryder learned a valuable lesson: not every dog is a threat, and not every situation requires a reaction. Also notice how Bishop's corrections increase in intensity throughout the video. He starts with the minimum amount of pressure necessary and only escalates when Ryder chooses not to listen. That's how dogs naturally communicate with one another. Will I tell these owners to take her to a dog park and expect her to be everyone's best friend? Absolutely not. But can we give her a better quality of life by helping her calmly walk past another dog across the street? Absolutely. Not every dog needs this type of training, but some dogs can benefit tremendously from it. If you're tired of dealing with an overly reactive dog, DM me "Bishop." #realdogtraining #fypsviral #belgianmalinois #fypreels #americanpitbullterrier

As it grows, gradually introduce fresh fruits, vegetables, nuts, and squirrel food. It brings together the best football clubs from European leagues to compete for the title of the best team in Europe. 🏁 History Founded: 1955 (originally called the European Cup) Renamed: UEFA Champions League in 1992 The original tournament was only for league champions, but today it includes the top teams from each country (for example, 1st–4th places in the Premier League, La Liga, Serie A, etc.). 🧩 Format of the Tournament 1. Qualifying Rounds Smaller clubs from lower-ranked European leagues play several knockout rounds in summer to reach the group stage. 2. Group Stage 32 teams divided into 8 groups (A–H), with 4 clubs in each group. Each team plays 6 matches (home and away). The top two teams from each group advance to the Round of 16, while the 3rd place drops into the Europa League. 3. Knockout Stage Round of 16 → Quarterfinals → Semifinals → Final Two-legged ties (home and away) until the final. The Final is a single match on neutral ground (decided before the season starts). 🌍 Qualification Example Each country has a certain number of slots based on UEFA’s coefficient rankings: England, Spain, Germany, Italy → 4 direct places in group stage France, Portugal, Netherlands → fewer direct spots Smaller nations → enter through qualification rounds 🏅 Trophy & Rewards The famous “Big Ears” trophy (because of its large handles) The winner qualifies for: UEFA Super Cup FIFA Club World Cup Automatic spot in next season’s group stage Prize money: over €100 million possible for the winner (including bonuses and TV rights) 🔥 Most Successful Clubs Club Country Titles Real Madrid 🇪🇸 Spain 🏆 15 AC Milan 🇮🇹 Italy 🏆 7 Bayern Munich 🇩🇪 Germany 🏆 6 Liverpool 🇬🇧 England 🏆 6 Barcelona 🇪🇸 Spain 🏆 5 Ajax 🇳🇱 Netherlands 🏆 4 Manchester United 🇬🇧 England 🏆 3 🧠 Interesting Facts Real Madrid won the first five European Cups (1956–1960). Have you ever craved something you’ve never even had before? 😂 I randomly thought, what if I turned potatoes into boba? And let me tell you… they’re SO chewy and delicious!  Potato Boba Ingredients 3–4 russet potatoes 1 cup potato starch Salt, to taste For the chili oil topping 1 tsp gochugaru 1 tbsp chopped parsley or green onions 1 tbsp minced garlic 1 tbsp soy sauce 2–3 tbsp hot oil 1. Steam or boil the potatoes until fork tender (I steamed mine). 2. Mash them while they’re still hot. Add the potato starch and salt, then knead into a smooth dough. If it’s too dry, add a little water. 3. Roll the dough into small boba-sized balls. 4. Boil until they float to the surface, then transfer them to cold water. Drain well. 5. Place the potato boba in a bowl. Add the gochugaru, parsley or green onions, garlic, and soy sauce. 6. Pour the hot oil over everything and mix until well coated.
